senses.gloss: --(Pratadvoca; Venkateswara, Ed.) a place in the यज्ञशाल where Nabha-agni is located. वा. २९. २१.
--the details of topical heads fur- nished. M. २९१. २८.
--the commander-in-chief of तारक's army; fought with Yama, Jambha and others; his head cut off by विष्णु's cakra. M. १४८. ३८; १५०. 1-४३; १५१. २६-36.
(I)--a परा god. Br. IV. 1. ५७.
--for शक्ति worship, described. Br. IV. ४४. ७६-9.

--(also graha शान्ति)--propitiation to planets. Three kinds of, all distinguished--ayuta homa, लक्ष homa and कोटि homa. Ritual is like the shield against bows and arrows; to be performed for attaining wealth, longevity and prosperity, as also to get rid of troubles. Even the posses- sion of a copy containing the three forms of ग्रहबलि frees [page१-562+ ३१] the members of the household from all diseases. Also known as graha यज्ञ. M. १७. ५६; २४. ४६; ९३. 2. to the end; ९४. 1-2; २३९. 1 and 4-5.
--the sun so-called. वा. ५३. २९.

--burnt offering to the nine planets: Sun to be located in the centre; presiding deity is शिव; red colour; food pleasing to, is rice cooked with sugar. Moon in the south-east; presiding deity पार्वती; white rice with ghee and sugar pleasing to: Mars to be located in the south; presiding deity is Skanda; red; याव pleasing to: Mercury to be located in north-east; presiding deity is Hari; yellow; food pleasing to, is milk and rice. Jupiter in the north; presiding deity is ब्रह्मा; yellow rice and curds pleasing to: Venus in the east; presiding deity is Indra; white; food pleasing to, is coarse sugar and rice. Saturn in the west; presiding deity is Yama; black; rice, seasamum and pulses cooked in milk pleasing to: राहु south-west; presiding deity is काल; black; mutton food to: Ketu in north-west; presiding deity is Citragupta; smoke colour; coloured rice as food to:
1: M. ९३. 5-२०.
Homa detailed;
2: M. ९३. २१-84.
Icons of.
3: M. ch. ९४.
--interplanetary distances described. Br. IV. 2. १३१-4.
--a son of the third सावर्ण Manu. Br. IV. 1. ८१. [page१-563+ २९]

(I)--a village; outside the खेट; between the village and खेट is (1/2) yojana; the limits of boundary are two क्रोशस् and of क्षेत्र (fields) four धनुस्; the roads of twenty धनुस् leading to twenty directions and also roads to ग्रामस् and roads on the limits, १० धनुस्; also राजपथ; four धनुस् for branch streets; two धनुस् between the houses. Br. II. 7. ९४ and १०५; वा. 8. १००; ६२. १७१; ७८. ५७; ८७. २८; ९४. ४०; ९८. ११९; १०६. ७३-75; Vi. 2. १३; ३६. 6.

(II)--as a present to learned men, as distinct from towns at the time of पृथु. ग्राम behind the forest and the forest behind the ग्राम explained by ययाति to अष्टक; reference to ascetics and sages who, as residents of village should not use forest produce, and as residents of forests should not use village produce; deserted during the time of anarchy. ^1 Br. II. ३४. ३९; ३६. १९७; III. 7. ३०८; M. १४३. 3; २४६. ४५. ^2 M. १०. ३२; ४०. 9-१३; ४१. 2; ४७. २५७.
--the kingdom to which Puramjana went by the आसुरि entrance of his city with his companion Durmada. भा. IV. २५. ५२.
(I)--a name of विघ्नेश्वर. Br. IV. ४४. ६९.
(III)--a class of celestial beings in attendance in pairs on the sun God in each of the six seasons. वा. ५२. 1. [page१-564+ २४]
(IV)--resides in the sun's chariot in the months of Caitra and Madhu. Vi. II. १०. 3.
--a class of यक्षस्. भा. XII. ११. ४८; Br. I. 1. ८३; II. २३. 1 and १४.
--the village messenger, unfit for पन्क्ति भोजन। Br. III. १९. ३०; वा. ८३. ६१.

--cows, goats, men, sheep, horses, mules and horses at the commencement of त्रेता yuga; आरण्यस्, dogs, two-hoofed elephants, monkeys, birds, undakas and snakes; sapta ग्राम्य pas4ava, सप्ता aran2yakas (Tait. Samh.). Br. II. 8. ४७-49; वा. 9. ४६-8.
--a mind-born mother. M. १७९. १५.

--१४ kinds of corn; vritri, yava, माष, गोधुमा, अणु, tila, priyangu, कुलत्थिका, स्यामक, निवारस्, jartila, gavedhuka, kuruvinda, वेणुयव (bamboo corn) and मर्कटक. They originally grew unploughed and un- sown, but in the त्रेतायुग they were raised by the plough and by seeds. Br. I. 7. १३८, १४३ff.; वा. 8. १४४. १४. १५३-55. [page१-565+ २४]
--from the feet of नारायण; one of the १६ Ritviks for a यज्ञ. M. १६७. १०.
